relationships.subject: P2X4 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: These pain-related microglial P2X4 receptors are known to induce brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) production and release from microglia to modulate pain-transducing spinal circuits [67,68].

relationships.subject: 5-BDBD
relationships.evidence_quote: Developed as a negative allosteric modulator of P2X4 receptors, 5-BDBD, a benzodiazepine derivative, has been demonstrated to reduce pain behavior caused by chronic constriction injury in animal studies [69,70].

relationships.subject: adenosine A2A receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: the upregulation of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), a pro-inflammatory cytokine, is suppressed, while the anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin (IL)-10 remains upregulated in the spinal cord [29]

relationships.subject: P2X7 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: P2X7 receptors in microglia might be involved in the production and release of cytokines and chemokines, such as IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 3 (CCL3), and chemokines (C-X-C motif) ligand 2 (CXCL2) [84,85,86,87,88].

key_findings: Review: microglial P2X4 and P2X7 receptors drive neuropathic pain via neuron-glia interactions; P2X4 induces microglial BDNF release.
Purinergic receptors across the nociceptive pathway (P1, P2X, P2Y) are therapeutic targets with multiple antagonists/agonists in development.
